You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From d3381559497d453e254cd8cdbba88987c888f7bb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Daniel Schopf <schopf.dan@gmail.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2018 19:49:07 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] fix bug with global parameters introduced in c97482c

---
 src/potential_input_f0.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/src/potential_input_f0.c b/src/potential_input_f0.c
index 993b0c9..ee70b5e 100644
--- a/src/potential_input_f0.c
+++ b/src/potential_input_f0.c
@@ -846,7 +846,7 @@ void read_analytic_potentials(apot_state* pstate)
         int l = -1;
         for (int k = 0; k < apt->globals; k++) {
           if (strncmp(apt->param_name[i][j],
-            apt->param_name[g_pot.global_pot][k], strlen(apt->param_name[i][j])) == 0)
+            apt->param_name[g_pot.global_pot][k], strlen(apt->param_name[i][j]) - 1) == 0)
             l = k;
         }
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an incorrect comparison of string lengths when checking if `apt->param_name[i][j]` matches with the global parameter name `apt->param_name[g_pot.global_pot][k]`. The original code erroneously used the full length of `apt->param_name[i][j]` for the comparison, which could lead to mismatches due to the presence of a null terminator or additional characters at the end of the string. The patch fixes this by subtracting one from the string length, thereby correctly handling strings that may have been compared incorrectly due to stray characters.

    Code statements:
    <text1>

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an incorrect comparison of string lengths when checking if `apt->param_name[i][j]` matches with the global parameter name `apt->param_name[g_pot.global_pot][k]`. The original code erroneously used the full length of `apt->param_name[i][j]` for the comparison, which could lead to mismatches due to the presence of a null terminator or additional characters at the end of the string. The patch fixes this by subtracting one from the string length, thereby correctly handling strings that may have been compared incorrectly due to stray characters.
